title: Showcase Carousel and Reflection (Lab)
summary: Learners run a showcase carousel, give and collect strand-tagged peer feedback, and consolidate the term into a four-strand Emerging summary with one Term-2 goal.
objectives: Present the solution in a showcase carousel and give structured peer feedback.
Consolidate reflections into a Term-2 goal across the four strands.
Confirm the responsible-use message for every solution on display.

body: Welcome to the showcase. Today your class becomes a gallery of AI-supported solutions. You will present, learn from each other with honest feedback, and pull your whole term together into one clear goal for next time.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can present my solution in a showcase carousel and give structured peer feedback.
I can consolidate my reflections into a Term-2 goal across the four strands.
I can confirm my solution is responsible to use and honest about its limits.

terms.definition: A rotation where you present at your station and visit others.
Two things done well and one thing to improve.
To gather many notes into one clear summary.
No personal data, honest about limits, fair to users.
The next tier of skill you aim for in Term 2.

sections.heading: Feedback that helps
body: In the [[carousel]] you present in 60 seconds and then visit other stations. Leave '[[two stars and a wish]]', and tag each comment to a strand.
Good feedback is specific, kind and tied to evidence. A helpful wish is a gift, not a criticism.

sections.heading: Your term in one picture
body: Gather your feedback and notes into the four-strand summary: what you can now do in concepts, design and build, evaluate and use, and wider effects.
Then set one specific Term-2 goal toward [[Proficient]], and confirm every solution is responsible to use.

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
sections.heading: Let's try it - hands-on
body: Set up your station, present in the carousel, give and collect feedback, then consolidate your term into a four-strand summary and one goal.
items: Set up your station with your frozen solution, evidence and responsible-use message.
Present in 60 seconds with two justified choices.
Rotate to at least two stations and leave strand-tagged feedback.
Collect the feedback left at your station.
Set one Term-2 goal and confirm responsible use.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: What is the most useful wish someone gave you, and why?
How will you keep your future solutions responsible and fair?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: Write your four-strand summary, one line per strand.
Set one specific Term-2 goal that moves you toward Proficient.

questions.prompt: You are leaving 'two stars and a wish' at someone's station. Which wish is the most useful feedback?

options.text: Wish: your station was a bit boring to watch.
Wish: make it better before you show it to anyone else.
Wish (Wider effects): say who might be left out if the whole school used it, and how you would stop that happening.
Wish: I really liked your colours, well done!

feedback.correct: That wish is specific, kind and tagged to a strand, so the person knows exactly what to work on next.
feedback.incorrect: A useful wish names one thing to improve and which strand it belongs to — 'boring', 'make it better' and a compliment all leave the person with nothing to act on.

questions.prompt: Every station needs a responsible-use message. Which statements belong in that message? Select all that apply.

options.text: We do not store anyone's name or photo.
Our checker gets unusual items wrong about one time in five, so check its answer before you act on it.
We tested it with items from lots of different homes so it works fairly for everyone.
Our solution loads in under two seconds.
We chose a purple background so the station looks smart.

feedback.correct: Responsible use means no personal data, honesty about limits, and fairness to users — those three statements cover exactly that.
feedback.incorrect: Loading speed and the look of your station may be good work, but they say nothing about personal data, limits or fairness.

questions.prompt: Each carousel comment has to be tagged to a strand. Match each comment to the strand it belongs to.

left.text: Star: you explained clearly why your solution follows rules instead of learning from examples.
Star: your station showed a working prototype that sorts an item into a category.
Wish: try it on more items whose answers you already know, so your evidence is stronger.
Wish: say who might be treated unfairly if your solution was used everywhere.

feedback.correct: Tagging works by what the comment is about: explaining ideas, building the thing, gathering evidence that it works, or who it affects.
feedback.incorrect: Read what each comment actually praises or asks for — an explanation, a build, more testing evidence, or the effect on people — and the strand follows.

questions.prompt: A wish should be kept general and vague so that nobody feels criticised.

feedback.correct: Correct — good feedback is specific, kind and tied to evidence, so a specific wish is a gift rather than a criticism.
feedback.incorrect: A vague wish is kind but useless; being specific and tying the comment to evidence is what makes it helpful.

questions.prompt: Put the showcase carousel steps into the order that makes each step possible.

items.text: Set up your station with your frozen solution, your evidence and your responsible-use message.
Present your solution in 60 seconds with two justified choices.
Rotate to other stations and leave strand-tagged feedback there.
Collect the feedback other people left at your station.
Complete your four-strand summary and set one Term-2 goal.

feedback.correct: You can only give feedback once stations are set up and presented, and you can only summarise your term once your feedback is collected.
feedback.incorrect: The summary and goal come last, because they are built from the feedback you collect after presenting and visiting other stations.

formative.targets: Summative Term-1 task samples all four strands at Emerging; reflection informs Term 2
formative.check: Structured peer feedback across the carousel plus a completed four-strand summary and Term-2 goal
formative.successCriteria: Gives specific strand-tagged feedback, confirms responsible use, and sets one clear Term-2 goal.
formative.evidence: Feedback slips + completed four-strand Emerging summary with goal.
